notes:
Summary: Large e-commerce contact-center provider (outsourced + in-house agents). Primary ask = agent-assist + ticket summarization that remains reliable under incident bursts and seasonal peaks. Current stack: Amazon Connect + homegrown MVC for assist. Pain: last Black Friday they saw assist timeouts and cascading queue backpressure; agents reverted to manual searches => conversion & CSAT drop.

Key constraints / requirements:
- Latency SLO: suggestion latency <= 200ms p95 for in-call assist; summarization can be relaxed to 1-3s but must complete before wrap-up.
- Throughput: baseline 1.2k concurrent agents; seasonal peak up to 12k-15k concurrent during flash sales; expected token ingestion peak ~1M tokens/min across the fleet during worst-case.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to trade higher unit cost for firm availability during peak windows but needs predictable billing and cost model for committed capacity.
- Fallbacks: must have deterministic fallback to smaller models or cached answers; graceful degradation under queue backpressure is mandatory.
- Deployment: prefer VPC or on-prem control plane for audit + residency; need KMS integration and audit logs exported to SIEM.

POC scope: Redwood to demonstrate: 1) synthetic spike test at 10k concurrent agents with linear ramp, 2) failover to model-variant routing when latency/queue thresholds hit, 3) verify KV/prefix caching reduces token load for repeated queries, 4) show autoscaling warm-up strategy and pre-warming for predictable Black Friday-like events.

Quotes / snippets from calls:
- "We can't have the assist slow during checkout flash sales — conversion drops immediately." - Director of CX
- "Last outage created a queue backlog that took 2 hours to clear; agents were overwhelmed." - Ops lead

Security / compliance notes: Legal insists on data residency options for EU customers; security wants SOC2 + ISO evidence, plus KMS key control. We added a GitHub ticket for required compliance docs.
